failure_spatial_audit.slow_step_spatial_limitation: No step-472 position/velocity or per-iteration states were saved. Exact stall location or mechanism cannot be established from the existing evidence. Nearby saved states at 450 and 480 show the minimum determinant in the subsurface probe corridor; this does not prove why step 472 took 4,660 iterations.
failure_spatial_audit.recommendation: The clamp-interface remesh moved failure away from the clamp. These failing tets are well-shaped at rest but have 13.7–21.2 mm edges under a 20 mm diameter probe. One targeted interior/surface refinement trial is justified to assess spatial resolution; a generic quality pass is not supported, and refinement cannot yet be claimed to fix the trajectory.

legacy_port_setup_observation.bottleneck: Repeated faulthandler snapshots during a second setup were inside sparse._inverse_rows, constructing the exact factor. These timings precede the independent setup optimization and are not current-version performance claims.

interpretation: The matching-input penalty force and one-step update agree closely with executed native AlgPhD on the actual irregular original mesh, including contact states. This is stronger than comparing only iteration counts.
The unrounded original-source AlgPhD trajectory also inverts elements and permits deep penalty penetration. A tessellation match alone therefore does not establish a collision-safe full demo.

The original Python default method name selects generic PD in this C++ revision and failed at the first moving substep even without float32 conversion or coordinate translation. This is a separate method result, not an AlgPhD parity failure.
Signed-distance samples establish observed penetration only; they do not prove global nonintersection, and inverted volume meshes compromise inside/outside interpretation.

optimized_factor_equivalence.scope: Final production SparseInverse on original-mesh penalty-contact matrix against factors saved by an independent replay using the prior implementation. Complete CPU constructor timing is one sample with concurrent workloads.

current_asset_matches_tested_common_inpu.scope: Current post-rebake physical inputs are bitwise identical to the tested native fixture. Only provenance metadata and two display embeddings change.

limitations: The mesh experiment is not installed as the default asset. Better rest shape metrics are not proof of a positive full trajectory.

The spatially graded candidate is also not adopted: six well-shaped, finely resolved surface elements invert at rejected step424. Five already invert before the final contact correction. Improved tessellation alone did not fix the full motion.

Grid experiment loaded the staged contact-exchange module before its production integration, and the earlier factor implementation. Its source files changed on disk during the run; it is not labeled a frozen final-source run.
Full original-asset swept run uses unchanged final production source and rejects an inverted surface element at step480. Contact certification succeeds at that rejected step.
Sampled probe/surface overlap measurements are not exhaustive intersection proofs. Rejected steps roll back and do not advance the command clock.

Native AlgPhD full-cycle diagnostics use penalty contact; they are not validation of the optional swept extension. The original Python method name pd_eigen_alg4 dispatches to generic PD in the tested native revision.
Timing experiments ran alongside other workloads. CPU paired setup speedup is not GPU simulation FPS.
